name: addons
description: UNVERIFIED FIRST DRAFT -- blind-authored from a plain-language description only, never run against real hardware. Login into the app, close any post-login notification dialogs, view the Add-ons screen, then log out. Steps 1-7 (dismiss system dialog through submit) are copied from the already-proven test-cases/login.json sequence (bugs 18-23, closed out end to end on real BrowserStack hardware for both platforms); steps 8+ (notifications, Add-ons, logout) are new guesses about this app's UI and have NOT been confirmed against a real screen. Expect this file to need the same bug-by-bug correction login.json did -- run it once via PHOENIX_BATCH_MODES=test-case, PHOENIX_TEST_CASE_FILE=test-cases/addons.json, and report back whatever the log/report actually shows so the guessed steps can be fixed from real evidence, not another guess.

steps.instruction: tap the LOGIN button on the home screen to open the login form
steps.note: REMOVED the speculative "tap Allow" step (and its dedicated CLOSE-recovery) that used to run before this one. Across 8 real runs, a pre-login Allow dialog never once actually appeared here -- every attempt at that step was either a correct no-op skip or, twice (addons-run-android-6.log: the ACTIVATE SIM container; addons-run-android-8.log: the home screen's "More Icon", opening an unrelated More-menu overlay), the resolver confidently guessing a totally unrelated element instead of declining, each time blocking this required LOGIN step from finding anything. A step with zero confirmed real use and two confirmed real harms is pure liability -- removed outright rather than patched again. The two recovery steps below now have to cover both of this step's own confirmed mis-fire targets (ACTIVATE SIM's dialog, and now the More-menu overlay too), since this is the step actually prone to them.

steps.instruction: tap the CLOSE button to dismiss a popup asking to update the app to access a feature
steps.note: CONFIRMED real bug on addons-run-android-3.log, a different kind than the others: the home screen has two visually-similar unlabeled containers side by side (a plain View with a child TextView "LOGIN", and an identical-shaped View with child TextView "ACTIVATE SIM") -- this time the resolver's model picked the wrong one (ACTIVATE SIM), confirmed by the resolved xpath ending in View[2] instead of the View[1] a successful run used. Tapping it triggered an unrelated native "update the app to access SIM Activation" dialog (CLOSE/UPDATE APP buttons) instead of opening the login form. This is LLM resolution nondeterminism on an ambiguous pair of candidates, not a wording or sequencing bug like the others in this file. Recovery: close that dialog if it appears, then retry the LOGIN tap below (harmless no-op if the first tap actually succeeded, since the login form would already be open and this retry simply finds nothing to match).

steps.instruction: tap the More Close button to close the More menu popup
steps.note: CONFIRMED real bug on addons-run-android-8.log: the LOGIN tap above mis-resolved to the home screen's bottom-nav "More Icon" instead (accessibility id "More Icon"), opening an unrelated in-app menu overlay (SIM Status, Porting Status, Track Order, YesRoam Rates, Pay for Others) with a close icon of its own (content-desc "More Close"). A second confirmed mis-fire target for the same LOGIN-tap step, alongside the SIM-activation dialog above -- both get an optional dismiss step here before the LOGIN retry below.

steps.instruction: tap the LOGIN button on the home screen to open the login form
steps.note: Retry of the step above, only exercised when the first attempt mis-tapped ACTIVATE SIM or the More menu instead (see the two notes above) -- optional so it's a no-op once the login form is already open.

steps.instruction: type the phone number into the phone/account number field
tap the PASSWORD tab to switch the form into password-entry mode
tap the password field to focus it
type the password into the password field
tap the LOGIN button to submit the login form
wait for the login submission to finish and the notification-permission dialog to appear
steps.note: CONFIRMED real bug on addons-run-android-5.log, a timing race rather than a wording/sequencing/resolver bug: login submission shows a progress spinner for a variable amount of time before the native 'Allow MyYes to send you notifications?' dialog actually appears. On addons-run-android-4.log the dialog was already up by the time the two 'tap Allow' steps below ran, so both resolved fine. On this run it wasn't -- both Allow taps correctly found nothing (optional, skipped as no-ops) while the spinner was still showing, and by the time the NEXT step (tap Add-ons) ran, the dialog had finally appeared and blocked it, failing the whole run with 'No elements match' since that step isn't optional. No step-sequence fix could have caught this: the dialog's arrival time varies run to run. Added this fixed pause (needed engine support: a new 'wait' step kind in engine/test-case-runner.js, since nothing could previously pause between steps) to give the dialog time to show up before either Allow-dismiss attempt runs.

steps.instruction: tap the Allow button to dismiss a system permission dialog
steps.note: CONFIRMED real bug on addons-run-android-1.log: this app fires a native Android runtime-permission dialog ("Allow MyYes to send you notifications?", Allow/Don't allow buttons) right after login submit, not a custom in-app popup with a close/X button -- the original guess here ("tap the close or X button...") never matched it, leaving the dialog on screen and blocking the Add-ons tap underneath it. Fixed by reusing the exact, already-proven "tap the Allow button..." instruction from step 1 above (same resolver match, same dialog shape).

steps.instruction: tap the X button to close the coach mark tutorial popup
steps.note: CONFIRMED real bug on addons-run-android-2.log, MOVED here from after the Add-ons tap on addons-run-android-7.log's evidence: after dismissing the native Allow dialog above, the app shows a coach-mark tutorial overlay ("Your Account overview is easily accessible in the middle of the screen.", close icon ivClose, NEXT button btnNext) IMMEDIATELY on the post-login Dashboard/home screen -- not specifically after tapping Add-ons as originally assumed. Run 7's page-source confirmed this directly: the coach mark was already showing right after the Allow-dismiss step, before Add-ons was ever tapped. It happened to still work when placed after Add-ons in earlier runs only because the overlay persists across that navigation; moved here so it's handled at the point it actually first appears, and so a second blind "tap Allow" retry (removed -- see below) is no longer needed.

steps.instruction: tap the NEXT button on the tutorial popup to advance to the next page
steps.note: Fallback for when the single X tap above doesn't fully dismiss the coach mark: per direct screen confirmation, this is actually a multi-page carousel (8 dots visible: Dashboard, and presumably 7 more screens each with their own tip and NEXT button), not a single card. If X closes it on the first try, each of these NEXT taps below finds nothing on screen and is correctly skipped as optional (no-op). If X fails or only dismisses the current page, repeated NEXT taps page through the remaining cards until the carousel itself ends and the real screen underneath becomes tappable. Repeated 8 times below to cover the full carousel seen on screen.

steps.instruction: tap the NEXT button on the tutorial popup to advance to the next page
tap the NEXT button on the tutorial popup to advance to the next page
tap the NEXT button on the tutorial popup to advance to the next page
tap the NEXT button on the tutorial popup to advance to the next page
tap the NEXT button on the tutorial popup to advance to the next page
tap the NEXT button on the tutorial popup to advance to the next page
tap the X button to close the coach mark tutorial popup
steps.note: Final X tap in case the carousel ends on its last page with only a close/X control and no further NEXT (common pattern: last page swaps NEXT for 'Got it'/X) -- optional no-op if the overlay is already gone.

steps.instruction: tap the CANCEL button to dismiss a popup asking to turn on notifications in Settings
steps.note: CONFIRMED real bug on addons-run-android-7.log: a SECOND, different notifications prompt from the native 'Allow MyYes to send you notifications?' dialog above -- a custom in-app dialog titled 'Turn on Notifications' ('Notifications are turned off. Change your settings to allow notifications from MyYes app.', CANCEL/SETTINGS buttons) appeared after the coach-mark step, blocking the Add-ons tap below (the resolver correctly declined to misuse CANCEL/SETTINGS as an Add-ons match, unlike earlier runs' overconfidence bugs -- a good sign, but the dialog still needed its own dismiss step since Add-ons isn't optional). Tapping CANCEL, not SETTINGS, since the test should not navigate out to the device's system Settings app. This run also removed the previous second blind 'tap Allow' retry step, which run 7's evidence showed was actively harmful: with no second native Allow dialog ever confirmed to exist, that retry was resolving against the coach-mark screen instead (which has no 'Allow' button at all) and risked mis-tapping something on it -- the same resolver-overconfidence class as bug #7, this time removed at the source rather than patched around.

steps.instruction: tap the Add-ons tab or menu item
steps.note: CONFIRMED working on addons-run-android-2.log -- the guessed instruction resolved and clicked correctly; the run got past this step to the next (new) failure.

steps.instruction: tap the Profile or Account menu to find the logout option
steps.note: CONFIRMED working on addons-run-android-4.log: the coach-mark/carousel fix got the run all the way past Add-ons into the Profile tab (bottom-nav item, resource-id ivProfile/tvProfile), landing on a menu screen (Billing Info, E-Bills, FAQs, General, Get Help, Settings, etc.). The run then failed on the Logout tap below -- see that step's note.

steps.instruction: scroll down on the Profile screen to reveal the Logout option
steps.note: CONFIRMED real bug/gap on addons-run-android-4.log: the Logout tap failed with 'No LOGOUT or Log Out button found' even though the Profile menu resolved correctly one step earlier. The page-source dump at the point of failure shows the Profile screen's menu items (Billing Info, Coverage Map, E-Bills, FAQs, General, Get Help, IDD Rates, Network Status, Plan Details, Purchase History, Settings, YesCare, Ajak & Earn) sitting inside an android.widget.ScrollView, with no 'Logout'/'Log Out' text anywhere in the captured hierarchy at all -- i.e. it is off-screen below the fold, not merely unlabeled or mis-resolved like the earlier bugs in this file. This was a genuine engine gap, not a wording problem: executeSemanticAction only supported 'tap'/'type' until now, with no way to move the viewport at all. Fixed at the engine level (engine/semantic-act-executor.js: new 'scroll' action kind, a native mobile:scrollGesture/mobile:scroll gesture with no element resolution involved) and wired in here as one scroll-down step right before the Logout tap. Optional so it's a harmless no-op on a device/build where Logout happens to already be on screen.

steps.instruction: tap the LOGOUT or Log Out button to sign out of the app
steps.note: CONFIRMED real bug on addons-run-android-4.log: failed with 'No LOGOUT or Log Out button found on the screen' -- the button exists but is below the fold in the Profile screen's ScrollView (see the new scroll step above's note for the full page-source evidence). Not a wording or sequencing bug like the others in this file; needed a new 'scroll' capability in the engine itself, since one never existed before this fix.
